_comment: Public sector verticals: product safety recalls, political money and federal spending, from free US government APIs (CPSC, NHTSA, FDA, FEC, Senate LDA, USAspending, Treasury). Batch 2's one new service.
description: Scored US public sector briefs from official government data: product safety recalls (CPSC, NHTSA, FDA food), political money (FEC, Senate lobbying), federal spending (USAspending, Treasury), natural hazards (FEMA, USGS, NWS), cyber threat (CISA KEV, NVD), respiratory illness (CDC), wildfire activity (NIFC), climate anomaly (NOAA), air travel demand (TSA), federal rulemaking (Federal Register), legislation (Congress.gov), environmental enforcement (EPA ECHO), Medicare enrollment (CMS) and nonprofit finances (IRS Form 990). Each brief is a 0-100 score with label, trend versus the horizon, the inputs that drive it, risk flags, confidence and a citation for every input.

verticals.title: US product safety recalls
verticals.question: Are consumer product, vehicle or food recalls rising?
verticals.note: Higher score means calmer than usual: fewer recalls and fewer units recalled than each series' own trailing year, across CPSC consumer products, NHTSA vehicles and equipment, and FDA food (Class I = most serious). The largest recent recalls are listed under recent_events.

verticals.title: US political money
verticals.question: Is outside election spending or lobbying activity rising?
verticals.note: Higher score means more political money activity than usual: independent expenditure items reported to the FEC and new lobbying registrations, monthly, against their own history (about two years, so one federal election cycle). All lobbying filings posted is a watch item. Spending clusters before elections, so read the trend with the calendar.

verticals.title: US federal spending
verticals.question: Is federal spending accelerating, and in which agencies?
verticals.note: Higher score means faster federal spending growth than usual: award obligations (USAspending) and Treasury outlays, year over year. Receipts, the monthly deficit and obligations by the eight largest awarding departments are watch items, so the brief shows which agencies are unusual. Recent months fill in as agencies report.

verticals.title: US natural hazards
verticals.question: Are disasters, severe weather and earthquakes running above normal?
verticals.note: Higher score means calmer than usual: fewer FEMA disaster declarations and fewer earthquakes (magnitude 4+ in the US region, 6+ worldwide) than each series' trailing two years. Active severe or extreme NWS weather alerts are a daily watch item that builds history from the first run. Declarations and major quakes are listed under recent_events.

verticals.title: Cyber threat level
verticals.question: Are actively exploited software flaws rising?
verticals.note: Higher score means calmer than usual: fewer vulnerabilities added to CISA's Known Exploited catalog (all, and those used in ransomware) each week, and fewer critical CVEs published in the NVD each month, against their trailing history. All CVEs published is a watch item. The newest exploited vulnerabilities are listed under recent_events.

verticals.title: US respiratory illness
verticals.question: Is respiratory illness (COVID-19, flu, RSV) rising in the US?
verticals.note: Higher score means less respiratory illness than usual: the weekly share of US emergency department visits diagnosed as COVID-19, influenza or RSV (CDC National Syndromic Surveillance Program), each against its own trailing year. Seasonal: winter peaks are normal, so read the trend with the calendar. Not for clinical decisions.

verticals.title: US wildfire activity
verticals.question: Is the US wildfire season running above normal?
verticals.note: Higher score means calmer than usual: wildfire incidents reported and acres burned each month (NIFC WFIGS incident locations), against the trailing years. Strongly seasonal: summer peaks are normal, so read the trend with the calendar.

verticals.title: US climate anomaly
verticals.question: How far are US temperature and precipitation from normal?
verticals.note: Higher score means closer to normal: the monthly contiguous-US average temperature and precipitation departures from the 1991-2020 normal (NOAA NCEI Climate at a Glance). Unusually hot or cold, wet or dry all score low; the departures themselves are in each input's value.

verticals.title: US air travel demand
verticals.question: Are more people flying than a year ago?
verticals.note: Higher score means stronger air travel demand than usual: people screened at TSA checkpoints each week, year over year, against its own history. Holiday weeks shift between years, so a single week can swing.

verticals.title: US federal rulemaking
verticals.question: Is the federal government issuing more regulations than usual?
verticals.note: Higher score means more rulemaking than usual: final rules, proposed rules and significant final rules (Executive Order 12866) published in the Federal Register each month, against the trailing years. More is neither good nor bad; it measures regulatory activity. The latest significant rules are listed under recent_events.

verticals.title: Medicare enrollment
verticals.question: Is Medicare enrollment growing, and is it shifting to Medicare Advantage?
verticals.note: Higher score means faster Medicare growth than usual: total beneficiaries and Medicare Advantage (and other health plan) enrollment each month, year over year (CMS Medicare Monthly Enrollment). Original Medicare enrollment is a watch item, so the brief shows the shift between the two.

verticals.title: US legislation
verticals.question: Is Congress introducing and passing more bills than usual?
verticals.note: Higher score means more legislative activity than usual: public laws enacted and House and Senate bills introduced each month (Congress.gov), against the trailing years. Activity follows the session calendar and the two-year Congress, so read the trend with the calendar. New public laws are listed under recent_events.

verticals.title: US environmental enforcement
verticals.question: Is EPA enforcement activity rising or falling?
verticals.note: Higher score means more EPA enforcement than usual: civil enforcement cases with a milestone each month, those with a federal penalty, and judicial cases (EPA ECHO), against the trailing years. Federal penalties in cases settled that month are a watch item because single large settlements dominate. Cases are entered with a lag, so recent months fill in.

verticals.title: US nonprofit finances
verticals.question: Are US nonprofits' revenue, donations and assets growing?
verticals.note: Higher score means faster nonprofit growth than usual: total revenue, contributions and grants received, and year-end assets of Form 990 filers, and the number of returns, year over year (IRS SOI annual extracts, by IRS processing year, so about a year behind). Total expenses are a watch item.
